extDescription.message: One-click Bilibili frame capture at native resolution, without pausing. Save as PNG/JPG/WebP or copy to clipboard.

actionTitle.message: Capture the current Bilibili video frame

toastCopied.message: Copied to clipboard. Paste it into a chat or document.

toastCopyDenied.message: Copy failed (the browser denied clipboard access). Use "Save file" instead.

toastNoVideo.message: No video found (use this on a Bilibili watch page).

toastNotReady.message: The video hasn't loaded a picture yet. Play it for a moment, then try again.

toastAutoCopyFailed.message: Auto-copy failed. Preview opened; click "Save file".

popupSub.message: On a Bilibili watch page, click the button below, press the shortcut, or click the camera button at the bottom right of the player to capture the current frame.

popupNote.message: Clean frames are captured at the resolution currently playing, without player controls, subtitles or danmaku. To include subtitles or danmaku, switch the capture mode to "What you see" in Settings.

popupNotBilibiliOpen.message: This is not a Bilibili page. Open a video first.

popupNotBilibili.message: This is not a Bilibili page.

optIntro.message: All three ways to capture work the same: the camera button at the bottom right of the player, the keyboard shortcut, and the button in the toolbar popup. Capturing does not pause playback; the video keeps playing and the image is the frame at the moment you pressed.

optShortcutNotSet.message: Not set (set it on Chrome's shortcuts page)

optShortcutHelp.message: Chrome doesn't let extensions change shortcuts directly. Change it on Chrome's own page: click the button below → find "Bilibili Screenshot" → click the pencil icon → press the new key combination.

optCleanDesc.message: — the video's native resolution (1080p/4K stays at its original size), with no player controls, subtitles or mouse cursor. Highest quality.

optCleanFallback.message: If the browser blocks frame capture for a particular video, it automatically falls back to the "What you see" mode.

optVisibleDesc.message: — captures what is actually on screen, so subtitles are included, but resolution is limited by the window size; it works best in fullscreen.

optPreviewDesc.message: — shows a preview, then choose "Save file" or "Copy to clipboard". Not happy with it? Close it and capture again, with no wasted files.

optDownloadDesc.message: — downloads straight to your browser's download folder on each press; good for capturing many frames.

optCopyDesc.message: — copies on each press so you can paste straight into a chat, document or email (if copying fails it opens the preview instead, so the image isn't lost).

optFileNamesTail.message: . Copying to the clipboard always uses PNG (a browser clipboard limitation), regardless of the format chosen here.

optDrmDesc.message: Bilibili's paid movies and anime are DRM-protected — on those pages the browser blacks out the picture in both capture modes. This is an industry-wide restriction that no extension can get around. Regular Bilibili videos are not affected, and clean frames capture at the resolution currently playing, up to 4K.

optSubsDesc.message: clean frames contain neither subtitles nor danmaku — both are drawn by the web page over the video and are not part of the picture (subtitles burned into the video itself are part of the picture and do appear). To include them, use "What you see"; it captures at the size shown on screen, so capture in fullscreen for the best quality.

optScopeDesc.message: this extension works on video pages at www.bilibili.com only — not on live streams (live.bilibili.com) or other subdomains.

optVertical.message: Vertical videos work too (native vertical resolution).

optPaused.message: You can capture while paused; you get the frame that is on screen.

optSafari.message: Safari: this extension is standard Web Extension source and can be converted with Xcode's safari-web-extension-converter; see the Safari section of the project README.

optLangDesc.message: Applies immediately to the settings page, the toolbar popup and in-page messages. The extension name shown on Chrome's extensions page still follows the browser language (a Chrome limitation).
